title: Cellular Protein Extraction and Western Blotting Using Dry Transfer (iBlot System)
author: Ralitsa R Madsen
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.4r4gv8w
materials: Prepare the required materials for transfer: trays with EZ gel staining reagent, trays with double-deionised H 2 O for filter paper wetting, tissue paper, scalpel, forceps, transfer packs, iBlot2 machine.

steps.title: Pre‑chill equipment and prepare scraper
steps.instruction: Set the benchtop microcentrifuge to 4 °C. Prepare a cell scraper and a beaker filled with PBS for rinsing the scraper between samples.

steps.title: Make ice‑cold lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Aliquot 10 mL of stock lysis buffer, add the fresh supplements listed in the buffer guidelines, keep the solution on ice.

steps.title: Thaw snap‑frozen cells
steps.instruction: Place frozen cell plates on ice, thaw one plate at a time, then scrape each well on ice, rinsing the scraper in PBS between individual samples.

steps.title: Lyse cells
steps.instruction: Add 150 µL of ice‑cold lysis buffer per well (volume may be reduced to 100 µL for low‑yield lines), scrape the cells on ice, and transfer the lysates to pre‑labelled, pre‑chilled microcentrifuge tubes.

steps.title: Incubate lysates on ice
steps.instruction: Incubate the tubes on ice for at least 00:30:00.

steps.title: Optional nuclear sonication
steps.instruction: If extracting histones, sonicate the lysates on a Diagenode Bioruptor: 5 pulses of 00:00:30 ON / 00:00:30 OFF at high power. Lysates should appear clear after sonication.

steps.title: Centrifuge lysates
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 4 °C for 00:10:00. Discard the pellet and transfer the supernatant to new pre‑chilled tubes.

steps.title: Store cleared lysate
steps.instruction: Freeze the supernatant at –20 °C (stop‑point). Limit freeze‑thaw cycles to three, or aliquot to avoid repeated thawing.

steps.title: Dilute for protein assay
steps.instruction: Dilute each lysate 1:5 (or as needed) with molecular‑grade H₂O; dilute the lysis buffer the same way. Perform dilutions in PCR strip tubes.

steps.title: Prepare DC assay A+S master mix
steps.instruction: Mix 20 µL Reagent S with 1 mL Reagent A (Bio‑Rad) to make the A+S solution. Prepare a master mix in excess (e.g., 1920 µL ≈ 2 mL for 8 standards + 8 samples in quadruplicate).

steps.title: Add A+S to assay plate
steps.instruction: Dispense 25 µL of the A+S mix into each well of a 96‑well Sterilin™ Clear Microtiter™ Plate (Thermo Scientific #11349163).

steps.title: Add samples and standards
steps.instruction: Add 5 µL of each diluted sample or standard to the appropriate wells in triplicate (use a multichannel pipettor). Example layout is provided in the original text.

steps.title: Add Reagent B and develop
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL Reagent B to each well, wrap the plate in foil, and shake on an orbital shaker at 300 rpm for 00:15:00.

steps.title: Measure absorbance
steps.instruction: Read absorbance at 595 nm on a plate reader.

steps.title: Calculate concentrations and loading volumes
steps.instruction: Generate a standard curve, subtract the lysis‑buffer‑only blank, and calculate each sample’s concentration (e.g., G7_25 0.1487 mg/mL, G7_26 0.1324 mg/mL, … G7_33 0.1345 mg/mL). Determine the volume needed to load 10 µg of protein per well in 20 µL for midi gels (or 5 µg per well for 4‑gel loading: prepare 20 µg in 80 µL and load 20 µL).

steps.title: Heat samples
steps.instruction: Heat each sample at 70 °C for 00:10:00 (use a thermocycler if samples are in PCR strips). Cool to room temperature, then pulse‑spin to collect condensate.

steps.title: Prepare running buffer
steps.instruction: Dilute 20X MOPS or 20X MES stock with deionised water to working strength. For the inner gel chamber, add 500 µL NuPAGE Antioxidant per 200 mL of running buffer.

steps.title: Prepare blocking buffer
steps.instruction: Make 1X TBS/T containing 0.1 % Tween‑20 and 3 % (w/v) BSA.

steps.title: Run SDS‑PAGE gel
steps.instruction: Load 10 µL protein ladder at the start/end of each gel, load each sample (volume calculated above), and run at 120 V until the dye front reaches the bottom (≈ 02:00:00). Mix samples thoroughly before loading. Note: a midi tank holds up to 4 gels; use 12‑well gels or fewer for optimal loading.

steps.title: Transfer proteins with iBlot2
steps.instruction: Disassemble the cassette, trim excess gel, and transfer using the iBlot2 system (Program P3, 00:07:00). Wet filter paper in double‑deionised H₂O, tap‑dry on tissue, then place on the gel before assembling the stack.

steps.title: Cut, mark, and block membrane
steps.instruction: Cut the membrane as needed, mark its identity (e.g., corner triangles, gel number), place it in a container with blocking buffer covering the entire surface, and rock on a shaker for 45 min–1 h.

steps.title: Stain gel with EZ Blue
steps.instruction: Incubate the transferred gel in EZ Blue solution for 01:00:00 on a shaker, then destain with deionised H₂O on a shaker until the gel is clear. The gel can be imaged later at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare primary antibody dilutions
steps.instruction: Dilute the primary antibody in blocking buffer according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Incubate membrane with primary antibody
steps.instruction: Remove the blocking solution, add enough primary‑antibody dilution to cover the blot, and incubate at 4 °C with rotation, typically overnight.

steps.title: Store primary antibody
steps.instruction: Decant the used primary antibody into its original tube, supplement with 0.02 % sodium azide, and return to the refrigerator for reuse.

steps.title: Wash membrane after primary
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane 5 × for 5 min each with 1X TBS/T buffer.

steps.title: Prepare secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Dilute the secondary antibody 1:10,000 in blocking buffer (options: anti‑rabbit IgG HRP‑linked CST #7074S or anti‑mouse IgG HRP‑linked CST #7076S).

steps.title: Incubate with secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Cover the membrane with the secondary‑antibody solution and incubate for 01:00:00 at room temperature on a shaker, ensuring complete coverage.

steps.title: Store secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Decant the secondary solution and keep the tube in the fridge for one additional reuse if desired.

steps.title: Wash membrane after secondary
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane 5 × for 5 min each with 1X TBS/T buffer.

steps.title: Apply ECL detection reagent
steps.instruction: Prepare ECL solution as per the manufacturer (use 2 mL per 10 cm × 8 cm membrane). Place the membrane on a flat surface, drain excess wash, and evenly apply the ECL mix.

steps.title: Develop chemiluminescence
steps.instruction: Incubate the membrane with ECL for 00:05:00, then image using a chemiluminescence imaging system. Record imaging settings in a readme.txt file together with sample, transfer, and antibody details.

steps.title: Store developed membrane
steps.instruction: Keep the membrane in 1X TBS/T at 4 °C for up to two weeks for possible re‑probing.

steps.title: Vortex samples briefly
steps.instruction: Vortex each sample for 00:00:05 before loading.

steps.title: Thaw BSA standards
steps.instruction: Thaw previously prepared BSA standards (0 – 2 mg/mL) for the DC assay.

steps.title: Load samples onto gel
steps.instruction: Using gel‑loading tips, load each sample (and 10 µL protein ladder) onto the gel. Run at 120 V until the dye front reaches the bottom (≈ 02:00:00).

steps.title: Note tank and gel orientation tips
steps.instruction: A midi tank holds up to 4 gels; loading is easier with 12‑well gels or fewer. Avoid loading gels backwards to reduce sample diffusion.
